messages:
kira: Heads up, immediate action required — our automated signing telemetry picked up suspicious usage of the internal code-signing key for `redwood-runtime` yesterday evening. We need a coordinated rotation + audit window. More details below.
sec-bot: [AUTO] Alert: anomalous code-signing activity detected on key `cs-rt-prod-1` 2026-03-20T19:42:03Z. Unusual subject: CI runner from eu-west-1. Link: https://security.redwood.internal/alerts/AGO-3342
sam: Yikes. Any indication this was an exfil or just misconfigured CI?
kira: Not yet confirmed exfil — logs show a runner spawned with stale token. We need to rotate the private key, revoke tokens that can access it, and run a one-hour signing freeze window for new releases.
maria: What’s the blast radius for the rotation? CI, deployed binaries, package signing? Need to notify partner integrators.
jordan: Blast: signing key used by our Linux and macOS build pipelines and the release CDN signing step. Rotating key requires updating KMS secret and CI secrets, then re-signing any builds we want to trust. Old binaries remain verifiable against the old public key until we publish the new key's delegation.
lee: Steps I propose: 1) create new key pair in KMS (policy: offline generation + HSM wrap). 2) update `ci/secrets/cs-rt-prod` with new private key id. 3) rotate signing service to new key, keep old key active for verification only for 7 days. 4) revoke any runner tokens issued in last 48h.
kira: Timeline: start rotation now (within 2h). Maria — please prepare comms for partners saying a maintenance window will occur. Jordan / Sam / Lee — coordinate on the PRs. Oncall-ops, be ready for rollout rollback.
oncall-ops: Acknowledged — paging oncall and will standby. If we need to cut a hotfix, tag me.
devops-bot: CI policy patch created: https://git.internal/redwood/ops/merge_requests/2189 — will block new releases until rotation completes.
sam: Recommended commands to revoke runner tokens and identify candidates: ```
# list tokens last 72h
redwoodctl tokens list --scope=runner --since=72h
# revoke token
redwoodctl tokens revoke <token-id>
# identify sign events
redwoodctl signing events --key cs-rt-prod-1 --since=48h
```
kira: Security asks each service owner to post a one-line confirmation in this thread after they've completed their step: created KMS key, updated CI secret, restarted signing service, revoked tokens. We'll collect audit proofs.
maria: Draft comms for partners: "We’re performing a precautionary key rotation for the code-signing service. There will be a temporary pause on new releases (<=1h). No evidence of compromise of customer data. We’ll follow up once rotation completes." Sending for legal review now.
jordan: I’ll handle KMS + signing service switchover. ETA 40m.
lee: Updating CI secrets now. Will post confirmation when done.
oncall-ops: If anything fails, use rollback plan: set signing service to verification-only mode and re-enable old key. Have rollback playbook at https://runbooks.redwood.internal/signing-rollback
sec-bot: [AUTO] Note: we also flagged two anomalous SSH sessions from build-runner-3 in eu-west-1. Security team will open a separate incident ticket if we see evidence of breakout.
kira: Thanks everyone. Please keep messages short — we’ll do a quick postmortem after containment. :lock:
